title: Preoperative Indocyanine Green administration increases intraoperative detection of Liver Tumors in Imaging-guided surgery. A phase IV clinical trial.
official: Preoperative Indocyanine Green administration increases intraoperative detection of Liver Tumors in Imaging-guided surgery. A phase IV clinical trial.
summary:
Main objective: •	To analyze the detection of liver tumors using indocyanine green fluorescence uptake in combination with intraoperative ultrasonography and preoperative imaging test
•	To develop a machine-learning algorithm to detect liver tumors with indocyanine green by photographic analysis.
conditions: Patients with liver tumors that will undergo minimally invasive liver surgery
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients with liver tumors with an indication for minimally invasive surgery, evaluated by the hospital’s multidisciplinary liver tumor board (MDTB).
2. Preoperative imaging test (contrast-enhanced liver MRI, multiphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT, or contrast-enhanced PET-CT) performed prior to the surgical intervention according to usual clinical practice of each site.
3. ≥18 years old
4. Absence of exclusion criteria and able to provide consent for data collection and analysis
Exclusion criteria:
1. Emergency surgery
2. Patients in which ICG is contraindicated (one condition will be enough for excluding the patient): 1.	previous history of iodine hypersensitivity; 2. patients with renal failure (GFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2); 3 uremic syndrome; 4. clinical hyperthyroidism; 5. autonomic thyroid adenomas; or 6. focal and diffuse autonomic abnormalities of the thyroid gland.
3. Previous liver surgery
